sources.citation: Aarssen, Anne; Genis, Rene; van der Veeken, Eline (eds.) (2018). A Bibliography of Sign Languages, 2008-2017. Leiden: Brill (Permanent International Committee of Linguists).
sources.note: Bibliographic record only: its section 1.2.1 'Suprasegmental phonology (prosody)' contains no Chinese Sign Language item; the ten CSL-indexed entries are lexicon, negation, numerals, education and neuroimaging works (e.g. Yang 2016 numerals; Fischer & Gong 2010).

sources.citation: Lin, Hao; Jiang, Yi; Gu, Yan (2024). Prosodic marking of information status in Chinese Sign Language. Proceedings of Speech Prosody 2024 (Leiden), 856-860. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2024-173
sources.note: Instrumental discourse study, not a phonology: 32 CSL signers' sign durations shrink over repeated mentions (M1 667 ms to M3 398 ms) as a prosodic cue to givenness; mentions in passing that in sign languages 'tension and large articulation and the lengthening of signs' are prosodic means, but gives no statement about lexical/word-level stress placement in CSL. The word 'stress' does not occur.

sources.citation: Sandler, Wendy (2010). Prosody and syntax in sign languages. Transactions of the Philological Society 108(3), 298-328 (PMC3250094).
sources.note: Mentions Chinese Sign Language only for negation (Yang & Fischer 2002); nothing on CSL stress.
